validity.recommendation: Keep the row; it is a real, correctly-classified line. Address the attribution and capacity concerns filed separately.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE = CONFIRMED (high, 3 independent). The line is a real 24-inch gas trunk carrying Western Desert field gas to the Ameryia (El Amreya) coastal distribution point west of Alexandria. (1) The sheet's origin source — egyptoil-gas.com 'Western Desert' PDF (2020) — lists in its Western Desert natural-gas table a line 'BED/AS-Ameryia', From 'BED/Abu Sennan connector' To 'Ameryia', Length 160 km, Diameter 24 in, Capacity 350 mmcf/d; GEM transcribed that row exactly. (2) INDEPENDENT: petro-news.com/125650 (Sept 2022) reports an illegal-drilling incident directly over 'the 24-inch gas line coming from the Badr El Din fields heading to the Ameryia gas station' (خط الغاز بقطر 24 بوصة القادم من حقول بدر الدين والمتجه إلى محطة الغاز بالعامرية), confirming it exists and is operating. (3) GulfPub PE World Map carries 'BAPETCO Pipeline', Alam El Shawish -> Ameriya Refinery, dia 24, operator BAPETCO — the same 24-inch BED-area-to-Ameriya line. CLASSIFICATION = CONFIRMED: a 160 km, 24-in field-to-coast trunk feeding the Ameryia distribution/processing area = gas transmission, not gathering/plant-internal, not oil/NGL. DUPLICATE = none in GEM: related roster rows are distinct upstream/parallel lines — P3937/P3938 (Badr El Din Spur 1/2) feed INTO the BED/Abu Sennan connector per the same PDF table, P6689 (Abu Sennan Spur) is the 14-in GPT feeder, and P3934 (PDF 'Tarek-Ameryia', 231 km/34 in/950) is a separate northern trunk; none is the same pipe as P3936. DIAMETER 24 in = CONFIRMED high (PDF + petro-news + GulfPub all agree). Length 160 km is single-source (PDF only; not independently corroborated — GulfPub's 97 km is measured from Alam El Shawish, a different origin) — caveat, not contradicted.

validity.recommendation: Re-examine owner/operator. Likely operator is BAPETCO (Badr El Din gas); GPC runs the Abu Sennan processing hub. Verify before keeping Owner=General Petroleum Company [100%].
validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists Owner AND Parent = General Petroleum Company (GPC) [100%]. This is single-source-inferential: the egyptoil PDF never states an owner for this specific line — it only says 'General Petroleum Company (GPC) established a plant for gas and condensate processing in Abu Sennan (~85 mmcf/d)'. Two independent sources instead attribute the LINE to Badr El Din Petroleum Company (BAPETCO): petro-news.com/125650 names BAPETCO as the party that halted the encroachment and inspected the line, and GulfPub tags the equivalent 'BAPETCO Pipeline' to operator BAPETCO. Separately, nsenergybusiness lists the Abu Sennan CONCESSION operator as Kuwait Energy Egypt — so at least three operators touch this corridor (BAPETCO for BED gas, GPC for the Abu Sennan gas plant, Kuwait Energy for the Abu Sennan oil concession). Owner vs operator is being conflated. Recommend: likely operator = BAPETCO; owner uncertain. Do not silently keep GPC 100% ownership.

validity.recommendation: Verify capacity. GEM's 350 MMcf/d is single-source (PDF) and directly contradicted by an independent source stating 200 MMcf/d. Reconcile before treating 350 as corroborated.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity 350 MMcf/d comes only from the egyptoil PDF table (BED/AS-Ameryia row). petro-news.com/125650 explicitly states the same 24-inch Badr El Din -> Ameryia line has a capacity of 200 million cubic feet per day (قدرته 200 مليون قدم مكعب يومياً). GulfPub's Capacity_mmcfd is the 300 placeholder (ignored). So capacity is single-sourced at 350 with a direct independent contradiction at 200 — cannot corroborate the GEM value to the 2-independent target; it may be 200. Flagged, not silently passed. (Length 160 km is likewise PDF-only, but not contradicted — see the existence note.)

routes.start_name: Abu Sennan / Badr El Din (BED-AS) field connector, Abu Gharadig Basin, northern Western Desert
routes.end_name: El Amreya (Ameryia) gas distribution / industrial area, west of Alexandria
routes.corridor_desc: Runs roughly north-northeast for ~160 km from the Abu Sennan/Badr El Din field complex in the Abu Gharadig Basin (northern Western Desert) across open desert to the Ameryia (El Amreya) coastal industrial/gas-distribution zone just west of Alexandria. Endpoints are named and independently placed (Abu Sennan field lat/lon from peer-reviewed literature; El Amreya is a named town/industrial zone on the coast); the interior alignment is NOT published, so treat the corridor as an approximate great-circle band between the two endpoints, loosely bounded.
routes.researcher_notes: End = Ameryia gas station, from petro-news (line 'heading to the Ameryia gas station') and the egyptoil PDF ('To: Ameryia'); El Amreya coordinates ~31.01N/29.80E are defensible from the named town west of Alexandria (approximate). Start = Abu Sennan/BED connector; coordinates ~29.58N/28.58E derived from the published Abu Sennan field extent 'between latitudes 29°30'N and 29°40'N and longitudes 28°30'E and 28°40'E' (PMC12332090). No coordinates were invented; interior waypoints left empty because no route geometry is published.

summary: P3936 EXISTS and is correctly classified (24-in gas transmission trunk, BED/Abu Sennan -> Ameryia; confirmed by 3 independent sources); staged concerns: attribution (GEM owner GPC 100% vs BAPETCO per petro-news+GulfPub) and spec (capacity 350 PDF-only vs 200 in petro-news); route corridor suggested at medium (named endpoints, interior approximate).
